method: Re-reviewed the lesson against registered Docker run/none-network, Python resource/subprocess, gVisor and Firecracker sources; corrected overstated mount, egress, credential, process-tree, and probe claims; replaced stale ordinal references with routes; checked every Python fence compiles, ran the harmless L1 pid-only proof, executed the complete published Docker runner and probe commands with --pull=never, and compared the configured and deliberately weak fixture stdout byte-for-byte with the lesson. Local environment: Docker server 29.3.1; cached python:3.12-alpine digest sha256:1b668429b3511ab407d8e00648891631b0b1a4d7e15e3ca70f38ab5b91ad4ab4; Python 3.10.9. The W6 verifier passed 9/9; the preserved 2026-10-21 verifier passed 10/10. No provider or external network calls were made. Production build generated 401 pages; Pagefind indexed 401 pages / 15,446 words. Light and dark full-page screenshots were inspected at 1300px viewport: article width 792px, document scrollWidth 1300px, one rendered Mermaid SVG; both captures are 1300x12294. The only browser console error was the existing /favicon.ico 404.
limitations: The Docker checks exercise one local daemon and one cached image digest; they do not establish production host hardening, multi-tenant escape resistance, image provenance policy, or deployed egress enforcement.
The route-table probe does not prove firewall, host-control-plane, or loopback-service inaccessibility; no external connectivity was attempted.
The Python resource and subprocess notes do not validate a production launcher or process-tree cleanup on other operating systems.
gVisor and Firecracker were checked against their registered architecture sources but were not installed, run, or benchmarked.
Historical L0/L1/L2/L2b timings remain non-comparable summaries with no archived raw per-run logs or complete environment metadata.
